solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prepares for action — reason may follow

definitions.meaning: soldiers told to get ready for an attack are ordered to take up position this way
the phrase is completed by the word reason, giving the idiom meaning it is logical

explanation.surface: A commander readies the troops, and a justification may come afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: add 'reason' after the answer and you get the familiar idiom 'stands to reason'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who take up battle stations are ready for action, the military sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: A service the abstainer takes comfort in

indicators.note: the abstainer takes something, holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other
in reinforces that the comfort sits inside the abstainer

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
ease means comfort or relief

explanation.surface: A teetotaller finds solace in a nice set of crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal; EASE goes between the two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A service is a full set of matching crockery, such as cups, saucers and pot for tea.

clue.text: Loop-line quickly going North, then East

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A railway branch line runs quickly northwards and then turns east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loop-line' looks like railway jargon, but it defines a rope tied in a loop; 'going North' reads the word upwards, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's knot is a loop made in a line of rope, so the hyphenated phrase describes it.

clue.text: Suspect wrongdoing, let alarms go off

indicators.note: alarms going off suggests things going haywire, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Sensing something fishy, someone sets off the alarm bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' rearranges the letters of LET ALARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense that something dishonest or underhand is going on.

clue.text: Above and just behind the clock

parts.note: over means above, higher than
due means just or deserved, as in getting one's due

explanation.surface: Something sits above and slightly behind a clock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just behind' reads as a single phrase meaning slightly behind, but 'just' is a piece and 'behind the clock' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late is behind the clock, arriving after the expected time.

clue.text: It's out of town and out of the country

definitions.text: It's out of town and out of the country

parts.words: It's out of town and out of the country
parts.note: a residential district sits beyond the town centre yet is not rural countryside either

explanation.surface: A place that is neither in the city nor in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the country' suggests abroad, but it means not in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlying residential district lies outside the town centre yet is still urban, not rural.

clue.text: Good players may make bloomers

definitions.meaning: in a tennis tournament the top-ranked competitors are placed so they do not meet early
planted in soil, these grow into flowering plants

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests blunders or knickers, but here it means plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-ranked tournament competitors are placed in the draw, and garden grains grow into flowering plants.

clue.text: Age-old celebrations

parts.note: read literally, these are parties marking how old one has become each year

explanation.walkthrough: 'Age-old' looks like 'ancient', but it means occasions celebrating getting a year older.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual parties marking another year of a person's age are celebrations of growing older.

clue.text: Uncooked, filleted and lean

parts.note: raw means uncooked
boned means filleted, with the bones removed

explanation.surface: A piece of fish is raw, filleted and has no fat on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture hides a description of a gaunt, bony person or animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gaunt and bony-looking is lean, with little flesh on the frame.

clue.text: Promise father a part in the play

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a role is a part played by an actor

explanation.surface: Dad pledges to take a part in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: A prisoner released early gives a promise of good behaviour, the original sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Early release is granted on a prisoner's word of honour, so the word means a pledge.

clue.text: You're probably surprised when they go up

definitions.text: You're probably surprised when they go up

parts.words: You're probably surprised when they go up
parts.note: the hairy arches above the eyes lift when someone is astonished

explanation.surface: Something rises when you are taken aback.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the facial hair above the eyes is the classic expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Pretty girl in crimson and rose

indicators.note: the pretty girl sits in the crimson, inside its letters

parts.note: red is a colour like crimson
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A lovely girl dressed in crimson with a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise, as in rising up against authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up against rulers is to revolt, so rose in that sense matches the past tense.

clue.text: Coach building

definitions.meaning: to coach is to train or teach someone
a place of education is a building where pupils are taught

explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to train or teach, and an educational establishment is also a building.

clue.text: He looks for a way to sell his wares

definitions.text: He looks for a way to sell his wares

parts.words: He looks for a way to sell his wares
parts.note: a way is literally a road, where a hawker sets up a stall

explanation.surface: A salesman seeks a method of selling his goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a way' reads as a method, but it is literally a road where a vendor sets up a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawker selling goods from a stall on the road plies his trade on the public way.

clue.text: Extent of usefulness on board

parts.note: goods sitting on a board in a shop remain sellable only for so long

explanation.surface: How long something stays useful aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but the board is a shop's ledge where stock sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The period a product stays usable while stocked on a store's ledge is its usable duration.

clue.text: Board bring in a head ready to educate

indicators.note: the board brings the other piece into itself, holding it inside

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging
each means a head, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A board of governors brings in a new head teacher, ready to teach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' looks like a head teacher, but it means per person, as in prices quoted a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receptive to instruction is ready to be educated, able to learn.

clue.text: One who insists on giving direction to trout-catcher

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south, a direction
a tickler catches trout by gently stroking them in the water before scooping them out

explanation.surface: A demanding person instructs an angler on how to catch trout.
explanation.walkthrough: Trout tickling is an old poaching technique of rubbing a fish's belly until it can be lifted out by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who insists on exact rules is a perfectionist about them, a precise demander.

clue.text: Try to intimidate and upset Theatre Trust

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to bully and disrupt a charity running a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of THEATRE TRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicing menacing warnings is how one tries to frighten someone into compliance.

clue.text: Savings book

definitions.meaning: money put aside for later is a fund kept in hand
to book is to secure a seat or table in advance

explanation.definitionFit: Funds set aside are kept in hand, and booking a table means arranging it in advance.

clue.text: Check one's surrounded by others

indicators.note: one's is placed inside the others, enclosed by them

parts.note: the rest means the others
one's reads as one is, I being the Roman numeral one and S standing for is

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether one person is hemmed in by the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is': I for one plus S, placed inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to hold it back or withstand it.

clue.text: Scratches from use of manacle on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard, inside a ship, so the piece goes within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is on board
a cuff is a handcuff or manacle

explanation.surface: Handcuffs used on prisoners aboard ship leave scratch marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' places CUFF inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks scraped onto shoes or floors by wear are scratches and abrasions.

clue.text: Stuffed dates dished out

indicators.note: served or handed out, suggesting the letters are rearranged on the plate

explanation.surface: Stuffed dates are served to guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed' looks like a description of the dates, but it is the definition: full up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has eaten so much they are full is stuffed or satisfied.

clue.text: Vessel sunk at the bar

parts.note: a sailing ship wrecked on a sandbar, or really a large glass of drink downed in a pub

explanation.surface: A ship foundered on the harbour bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunk' means drunk down and 'bar' is a pub, not a sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall drinking glass for sherry or beer is a vessel whose contents are downed at a pub.

clue.text: Cat found in a pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard is a big wild feline
there are sixteen of these weight units in a pound

explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests an animal pound for strays, but it is the unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow leopard is a big cat, and a pound contains sixteen of these weight units.

clue.text: Vandalised relics to place in the cathedral

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sacred relics are damaged and then put somewhere in the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vandalised' rearranges the letters of RELICS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walkway around a courtyard is an architectural feature found in many cathedrals.

clue.text: He's lawless — a little grasping also

indicators.note: the little piece grasps the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a bit means a little
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: An outlaw is rather greedy as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' looks like a description of greed, but it is the container signal; 'He's lawless' defines an outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber operates outside the law, so he is a lawless man.

clue.text: It's half-day closing, mate!

indicators.note: half of the day name is kept, its second half dropped

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week
end means closing or conclusion

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper announces early closing for the afternoon to a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-day closing' is the old British custom of shops shutting one afternoon a week; here 'half-day' is the first half of FRIDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British for a pal or companion.

clue.text: Employees in steel-works making components

indicators.note: employees go in the other piece, inside its letters
works suggests something reworked or operated on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: men are workers or employees

explanation.surface: Workers in a steelworks are making parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steel-works' reads as a factory, but 'works' is the anagram signal, making ELETS, and 'in' sets the workers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic constituent parts of a whole are its components or building blocks.
